title: dedicated-autoscaler: smoother burst smoothing and utilization reporting enhancements
author: Priya Raman
description: Context: Customers running dedicated fleets with bursty traffic observed repeated micro-scale ups and downs during short traffic spikes. This PR implements a smoother token-bucket smoothing mechanism, improves burst controls to avoid premature throttling, and expands utilization reporting to surface transient queueing that previously masked inefficient scaling. Motivation: reduce unnecessary scale-ups, improve tail latency during bursts, and provide ops teams better visibility for tuning policies. Changes: 1) Autoscaler: introduce a configurable smoothing window (default=30s) for token-bucket refill rate sampling and a leaky-integrator to prevent oscillation; 2) Burst controls: differentiate short-duration bursts (<=15s) from sustained load and allow controlled burst credit consumption without triggering immediate scale-up; 3) Backpressure: add a lightweight request admission signal from scheduler to autoscaler to signal persistent queue growth; 4) Utilization reporting: new metrics (dedicated.fleet.queue_depth_peak, dedicated.fleet.burst_credit_used, dedicated.fleet.smoothing_window_effective) and an aggregated per-fleet 1m/5m/1h utilization snapshot endpoint; 5) UI/observability: dashboard panels and alert rules for burst-credit exhaustion and sustained queue growth; 6) Config: new flags in fleet config (burst_short_threshold_secs, smoothing_window_secs, enable_backpressure_signal) and migration notes. Tests & perf: added unit tests for smoothing math, end-to-end integration test in perf-canary that simulates a Poisson burst workload, and a load test demonstrating a ~38% reduction in unnecessary scale-ups in our staging fleet. Rollout plan: feature-flagged, gradual canary to 5% fleets, monitor dedicated.fleet.scale_events and tail latency for regressions. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked ENG-1987 - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration/perf tests added - [x] doc updates (config + release notes) - [x] UX dashboard panels added - [x] telemetry events wired - [x] rollout automation for feature flagging Commits summary: several focused commits consolidating smoothing algorithm, telemetry, and config. See commits field for details. Files changed (high-level): autoscaler/service.go (smoothing + backpressure), autoscaler/tokenbucket.go (refactor), scheduler/admission.go (backpressure signal), telemetry/metrics.go (new metrics), api/v1/fleet_utilization.go (new endpoint), webapp/dashboards/dedicated_burst.json, configs/defaults.yaml, tests/autoscaler_smoothing_test.go, perf/perf_canary/burst_scenario.yaml. Backwards compatibility: default config preserves previous behavior until smoothing_window_secs is enabled via feature flag (off by default). No breaking changes expected. Migration: operators can tune burst_short_threshold_secs to match workload. See release_notes for ops guidance.

release_notes: Improved autoscaler stability under bursty workloads: smoother token-bucket sampling reduces oscillatory scale-ups, short bursts are handled with controlled burst credit consumption, backpressure signal prevents blind scale-ups due to transient queueing, and new utilization metrics/endpoints give ops teams better visibility. Default behavior preserved; enable via feature flag to apply smoothing window.
